fulfillment_judgment.auxiliary_material: The study used time to treatment discontinuation (TTD) as a surrogate for progression-free survival and employed a retrospective cohort design. Overall antibiotic exposure at any time and timing relative to ICI were not associated with shorter TTD or OS in the general analysis. The authors note their results differ from earlier systematic reviews showing universal negative effects but align with recent mixed findings. No microbiome sequencing data was reported to confirm mechanistic drivers behind the specific antibiotic effects.
fulfillment_judgment.outline_action: Cite this study as primary evidence for antibiotic class specificity, highlighting the contrast between vancomycin and other agents. Search for at least one additional study comparing antibiotic classes to meet the quantitative success criterion, preferably in different tumor types or using standard PFS endpoints. In the writing, explicitly qualify the findings as observational and specific to melanoma, noting the need for mechanistic validation regarding gut microbiome changes.
fulfillment_judgment.remaining_gap: The success criterion requires at least two studies comparing different antibiotic classes, and this material represents only one study. Additionally, the findings are limited to stage IV melanoma and use TTD rather than standard progression-free survival, leaving uncertainty about generalizability to other tumor types or endpoints. The lack of microbiome data means the mechanism behind the class-specific differences remains inferred rather than proven.
fulfillment_judgment.useful_material: This study analyzed 876 patients with stage IV melanoma receiving ICI therapy and compared the impact of specific antibiotic agents on outcomes. The authors found that vancomycin exposure was associated with decreased time to treatment discontinuation (HR = 1.26) and worse overall survival (HR = 1.79). In contrast, exposure to metronidazole and piperacillin-tazobactam had no significant impact on these outcomes. This provides direct comparative evidence that not all antibiotics negatively affect ICI efficacy, identifying vancomycin as potentially harmful while suggesting others may be relatively safe in this cohort.

record_identity.title: 535 Impact of antibiotic timing and antibiotic type on immune checkpoint inhibitor efficacy in patients with stage IV melanoma
